title: Implement predictive autoscaler safeguards and immediate mitigation for Dedicated throughput collapse
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-23 08:12 UTC a Dedicated customer pool observed a rapid 48% sustained drop in throughput (requests/sec) and elevated tail latency. The autoscaler did not add sufficient workers for ~45 minutes, causing downstream queuing, increased p95/p99 latency, and customer impact across three enterprise tenants. Scope: single Dedicated region (us-west-2), three affected pools (pool-a, pool-b, pool-c), approximately 12 hours of degraded performance for some tenants. Detection: Alerting fired for p99 latency and queue growth, but autoscaler health alerts were suppressed because the metric used by the scaler had undergone an earlier smoothing-window change and stopped crossing the trigger threshold. Root cause hypothesis: regression introduced in autoscaler smoothing logic (EWMA window expanded from 10s to 60s) in PR #1257 plus a kernel scheduler change that increased short-lived request latencies. Together these changes reduced the autoscaler's sensitivity to sudden queue growth, delaying scale decisions. Immediate mitigations performed: 1) Manual headroom override (+30% reserved capacity) applied to affected pools at 08:45 UTC. 2) Emergency rollback of EWMA smoothing change (reverted PR #1257) at 09:20 UTC. 3) Temporary autoscaler guard (min_workers_per_pool) enforced to ensure baseline capacity. 4) Hotfix PR #1309 deployed to reduce decision latency and add a short-circuit for >70% sustained queue growth. Post-incident verification: traffic replay and synthetic bursts show autoscaler now responds within 30s to comparable surges. Long-term plan: Implement predictive autoscaler safeguards and telemetry improvements (see action items). Goals: avoid regressions that mask genuine queue pressure, add conservative guardrails to preserve SLAs, and enable proactive scaling using short-term prediction. Success criteria: no Dedicated pool experiences >15% throughput degradation with similar surge patterns in chaos tests; autoscaler decision latency <= 30s for synthetic bursts; new telemetry and alerts cover at least 95% of observed pre-incident signals.

notes: Avoid over-reactive scaling: predictive model must include hysteresis and cost-sensitivity thresholding. Keep conservative defaults for enterprise pools. Coordinate with Sales/CS for any capacity-impacting defaults changes.
